title: Digital Marketing Strategy for Small Business | KivoReach
description: A simple digital marketing strategy for small businesses and beginners: set goals, know your customer, pick a few channels, publish and measure.

article.summary: A digital marketing strategy does not need to be long. Here is a one-page plan a small business can write in an afternoon and actually follow.
takeaways: Start from one or two business goals, not from a list of channels.
Pick the few channels your customers already use and do them well.
Measure from the start with free tools such as Google Search Console, and review monthly.
article.author: KivoReach

blocks.text: Digital marketing strategy for small business: a simple plan

blocks.html: A digital marketing strategy is a plan for how your business will reach and win customers online: who you want to reach, where, with what message, and how you will know it works. For a small business or a beginner, the best strategy is short, specific and realistic about time and budget.

blocks.caption: Five questions that make up a basic strategy
headers: Example answer for a local bakery
rows: Parents and offices within 10 km, planning birthdays and events
Google Search and Maps, Instagram, WhatsApp
Order online by 5 pm for next-day pickup; photos of real cakes
Pre-orders per week, website visits from Google, calls from the Business Profile

items.title: Set one or two goals
items.html: Tie them to the business: more enquiries, bookings or sales of a specific service. "Be on social media" is an activity, not a goal.

items.title: Describe your customer
items.html: Who they are, what problem they have, the words they search with, and what makes them choose you.

items.title: Fix your home base
items.html: Your website and Google Business Profile are where every channel sends people. Make sure they load fast, work on phones and make the next step obvious.

items.title: Pick two or three channels
items.html: Choose the ones your customers already use. It is better to do two well than six badly.

items.title: Plan simple content
items.html: Answer your customers' common questions, show your work, and share offers. A small, steady schedule beats bursts.

items.title: Measure and adjust monthly
items.html: Check what brought visits and enquiries, keep what works, and drop what does not.

blocks.caption: What each channel is good for
rows: People actively looking for what you offer
Time, and money if you boost posts
Time and an email tool; only email people who agreed to it

blocks.text: How to measure without paying for tools

blocks.html: Google Search Console is free and shows which searches bring people to your site, which pages appear in results and any problems Google finds. Your Business Profile shows calls, direction requests and website clicks. Write down the numbers once a month in a simple sheet next to your goals.
Be careful with promises of fixed results. No one can guarantee rankings or sales, and Google states that it does not accept payment to rank a site higher in its search results.

items: One or two goals written down, tied to sales or enquiries
A short description of your main customer and the words they use
Website and Business Profile ready to receive visitors
Two or three channels chosen, with a realistic weekly time budget
A simple content plan for the next month
Search Console set up and a monthly review in the calendar

blocks.question: How much should a small business spend on digital marketing?
blocks.answer: There is no standard figure that fits every business. Start with the time you can give every week, and add a small, fixed ad budget only for a clear goal you can measure.

blocks.question: Should I do SEO or ads first?
blocks.answer: Many small businesses do both: ads bring visits now, while SEO builds visits that do not cost per click. If the budget is zero, start with your Business Profile and the on-page basics of your website.

blocks.question: How often should I change my strategy?
blocks.answer: Review it monthly and change the plan when the numbers show something is not working. Change the goals only when the business changes.
